required_observations: The service is released, receives writes continuously, and has external v1 clients and durable identifiers.
The one-subscription-per-customer data ownership assumption conflicts with the target one-to-many model.
The public API and subscription identifiers are compatibility baselines, while internal storage layout is not.
The accepted target retains the service process and data-access boundary and rejects a parallel service with duplicated identity and distributed write ownership.
required_decisions: Evolve the released service in place by introducing target subscription ownership behind a data-access seam and moving an end-to-end slice rather than replacing all reads and writes at once.
Define canonical ownership, backfill, concurrent writes, idempotency, reconciliation, stop signals, and the actual rollback or forward-recovery window.
Plan expand, migrate, and contract phases that remove embedded subscription state and transition-only dual behavior only after their separate acceptance and action-local authority gates.
anti_findings: Do not recommend a single big-bang data cutover because the target model is cleaner.
Do not recommend a parallel target service when the accepted architecture retains the current service boundary and rejects distributed write ownership.
Do not treat a database backup or binary rollback as proof that writes can be reversed.
Do not let dual writes or the v1 adapter become an unowned permanent architecture.
safety_requirements: Planning is read-only and performs no production or fixture data mutation.
Deployment, external client movement, and irreversible contraction require separate owner authority.
